units.title: Make first contact
units.description: Greet, exchange names, and choose familiar or polite address.

lessons.title: Begin and end an exchange
lessons.outcome: I can greet someone and take leave.

familiar-greeting.title: Greet a friend

polite-greeting.title: Open a polite daytime exchange
polite-greeting.body: Use buongiorno when beginning this polite daytime exchange. Arrivederci is for leaving.

farewell.title: End the exchange
farewell.body: Arrivederci is a polite goodbye. The person is leaving, so this is a farewell rather than an arrival greeting.

lessons.title: Complete a first supported exchange
lessons.outcome: I can greet a peer, give a name and origin, ask for repetition and close the exchange.
lessons.takeaway: Respond with your own information: An introduction gives your own name with mi chiamo and origin with sono di. E tu? gives the other person a turn. Piacere is a friendly meeting phrase, not a name or a place. Ask for help, then close: When you miss a message, ask for a repeat rather than guessing a name. Può ripetere, per favore? is a taught polite chunk. At the end, arrivederci is a polite goodbye; a domani is appropriate when you expect to meet tomorrow.

forms.description: An introduction gives your own name with mi chiamo and origin with sono di. E tu? gives the other person a turn. Piacere is a friendly meeting phrase, not a name or a place.

When you miss a message, ask for a repeat rather than guessing a name. Può ripetere, per favore? is a taught polite chunk. At the end, arrivederci is a polite goodbye; a domani is appropriate when you expect to meet tomorrow.

lessons.outcome: I can identify a familiar word from its sound before reading its spelling.
lessons.takeaway: Listen to the familiar word, then choose what you heard. Casa begins with hard c; cena with soft c. Ch keeps c hard in chiave and chiesa. The known meanings let you focus on sound. This checks listening to words, not the quality of your own pronunciation.
